findings.title: normalizer.py:1720 - a MALFORMED artifacts.metadata_json still aborts the WHOLE normalization run from a different column, and starves every document behind it
findings.claim: `existing_metadata = json.loads(document["normalization_metadata_json"] or "{}")` (normalizer.py:1720) sits INSIDE the `except Exception` handler but OUTSIDE every try, so it is exactly the P0 shape on a different column: a document whose parse fails AND whose existing normalized artifact row carries malformed metadata raises JSONDecodeError out of the loop.
findings.evidence: My probe V-r3 P6, scenario S1/S4: seeded one document with a healthy-at-insert artifacts row whose metadata_json = 'not json at all' and a primary file missing so the parser fails -> `escaped: true`, `JSONDecodeError`, `normalizer.py:1720 existing_metadata = json.loads(`, 0 artifacts on disk. S4 is the blast-radius proof: TWO documents seeded, the second healthy and queued behind -> still `escaped: true` at 1720, 0 artifacts on disk, so the healthy document is never normalized. S5 control (same malformed artifact metadata but a HEALTHY parse) -> escaped=false, completed=1, proving the handler is the only route. The column is written only by normalizer.py:1833 (canonical_json, always valid) and artifact_backfill, so this is a latent/robustness hole today rather than an everyday production crash - which is why it is P2 and not P1. Note the sibling defect on the SAME line family is one I did NOT reproduce: `_atomic_write(output_path, content)` at 1766 is likewise outside the try.
findings.impact: One document with a damaged artifact row stops the batch: no ProcessingReport, no per-document failure record, no attempt counting, and every queued document behind it is silently unprocessed while the operator sees a traceback instead of progress.
findings.suggested_disposition: One-line change: `existing_metadata, _ = metadata_state(document["normalization_metadata_json"])`. The chain already degrades malformed text, None and non-object payloads to {} and metadata_state is already imported in this module. Then extend the P0 probe with this column as a third phase, and consider wrapping the artifact write too.

findings.title: The new GATE_BOUNDARIES entry is accurate in its numbers but describes the rule's coverage as wider than it is, and the underlying tools/ count is an observation rather than an enforced zero
findings.claim: read_chain.GATE_BOUNDARIES['readers_outside_the_scanned_roots'] says 'a second hard rule covers the REST of the product package and currently finds ZERO readers there ... `tools/` has 0'.
findings.evidence: `tools/` and `scripts/` are NOT under `src/company_wiki`, so the rule's PACKAGE root cannot see them by construction. Measured: injecting a direct reader into `tools/` -> 'test_b10_no_direct_reader_outside_source_catalog' still 1 passed; injecting the same shape into `scripts/` -> 1 passed. My own scan agrees with the numbers (tools/ 0 of 7 files, scripts/ 2 of 126) but shows the tools/ zero has no ratchet behind it: nothing fails if a tools/ reader is added tomorrow. The entry also omits `build/lib/company_wiki/**`, which contains stale copies of normalizer.py/evidence_span.py (build output, not product source - a judgement call, but the entry does not say so).
findings.impact: Low and honest-in-intent: the entry does name the boundary and does say the scripts/ pair is unratcheted. But a future reader can take '0 in tools/' for an enforced guarantee when it is a measurement, and can take 'the REST of the product package' for 'everything under src/company_wiki' rather than 'the scanned package root'.
findings.suggested_disposition: Either widen the hard rule to tools/ (tools/ is 7 files and currently clean, so a zero rule costs nothing) or add one clause to the entry: '`tools/` and `scripts/` are outside the rule's root - their numbers are measurements, not guarantees'. Same one line covers build/.

findings.claim: Three separate places still carry pre-fix or pre-deletion statements about the sites this commit changed: (a) the CONFIRMED_DIRECT_READERS docstring, (b) the COLUMN_VALUE_HANDOFFS docstring, (c) the implementation record's own §7quater.
findings.evidence: read_chain.py:96-98 still reads '`normalizer` (both) - the parse sits in normalize_catalog's FAILURE path (a malformed column currently produces a per-document normalization-failure record with attempt counting); converging it to {} would change those records.' Both halves are now false: my P2/P6 probes show a malformed column produces a COMPLETED document (not a failure record) and that the parse is not in the failure path at all - which is precisely what B-VR-B10R2-02 established; only the EXPLICIT entry was retracted, not this docstring. (b) read_chain.py:117 still states the handoff counts are '13 scopes / 16 sites' while the registry it documents now holds 12 scopes / 15 sites (this commit deleted the `normalizer.py::_frontmatter` entry) - the comment went stale as a direct result of the fix. (c) b10-implementation.md §7quater line 157 still says '13 作用域 / 16 站点' for the same reason, and the §7quinquies disposition row claims "the file's numbers have been updated to the current 15 cases / 10 mutants / CONFIRMED 1" while §2's heading, §7bis, §7ter and §8 still print the old generations and the strings '15 用例'/'10 变异' appear nowhere except that row. (d) The same wrong 13/16 number and the same over-broad claim were then copied into the newest draft of the round summary, r4-final-status.md (commit b7f6847, landed after I started reviewing): line 18 says '`COLUMN_VALUE_HANDOFFS` **13 作用域 / 16 站点**' and line 19 says '`normalize_catalog` 的解析**不再**能中止整轮' - my finding B-VR-B10R3-01 shows a sibling parse in the same function still can. That draft is labelled 'to be finalized after B.VR-b10-r3', so it is the right place to take both corrections before it is finalized.
findings.impact: The registry is the artefact a future converger reads to decide what is safe to leave alone, and B-VR-B10R2-02's whole lesson was that a wrong reason keeps a defect. These are comments, so nothing breaks at runtime - but they are false statements about the current tree in a file whose stated purpose is to be the machine-checkable truth, and they are the same class of defect the previous round rated P1 in the same lines.
findings.suggested_disposition: Rewrite the docstring bullet to the measured truth ('a malformed column degrades to no metadata and the document still completes; it is on the chain now - reverted by M10 if it ever comes back') and correct 13/16 -> 12/15 in read_chain.py, in §7quater and in the r4-final-status draft, or mark §7bis/§7ter/§7quater/§8 as superseded in one line each.

findings.title: Stale line citations in the record itself (the round-2 finding's own residual, one revision on)
findings.claim: §7quinquies cites `normalizer.py:1725` as the line the missing-file abort escapes from, and '唯一 try 起于 1664、body 仅 1665-1679' as the current structure.
findings.evidence: Measured: the escape is at normalizer.py:1732 on f92fc71 (the `IngestService.ingest` call in the UnsupportedDocumentError handler) and at 1701 on 5ec18a5; 1725 is the retry arithmetic on 5ec18a5 and the artifact_id assignment on f92fc71 - never the cited statement. findings.title: The P0 probe's phase 2 reports two readings as one piece of evidence, and only one of them is caused by the fix
findings.claim: b10-p0-probe.txt prints 'has metadata_unreadable flag: True / verdict consistent: False / verdict unverifiable: True' and the record's §7quinquies row presents all three as the behavioural proof of the -03 fix.
findings.evidence: The probe's fixture is a .md file, and the plain-text parser returns no first page, so `assess_homepage_identity(None, ...)` returns 'unverifiable' with reason 'no_first_page_text' BEFORE any metadata logic runs - i.e. 'verdict consistent: False' and 'verdict unverifiable: True' would hold even without the fix. My own P3 matrix, run with a first page that contains the title, is what actually isolates the delta: pre-fix those same cells read 'verdict: consistent' with no flag; on HEAD they read 'verdict: unverifiable' with the flag. So the fix is real and I confirmed it independently - the criticism is only that the cited evidence does not by itself separate the two causes.
findings.impact: Low: the conclusion is true and my probes prove it. But 'the artifact was flagged AND the verdict was downgraded' reads as two independent confirmations when the second is overdetermined on that fixture, and this is the sort of over-claim the round-2 record was rejected for elsewhere.
findings.suggested_disposition: Add the first-page-bearing fixture (or the value matrix) as a third phase so 'downgraded BY this fix' has its own reading, and say in the record that the .md fixture's verdict is unverifiable for the parser reason too.

findings.title: Two more measured whole-run abort paths outside the batch's scope (registered here so the picture is complete, NOT introduced by this change)
findings.claim: (i) `_atomic_write(output_path, content)` at normalizer.py:1766 is outside every try. (ii) The unsupported-document handler's own `IngestService.ingest` at 1716 is outside every try, so a missing/changed primary file escapes as SourceManifestMismatchError at 1732 (the F-B10R2-MISSINGFILE shape).
findings.evidence: (ii) is measured in my P6 S2: two documents seeded, the first with a missing file and an extension with no parser -> SourceManifestMismatchError from 1732, 0 artifacts on disk, the healthy document behind it never normalized. (i) is an AST/read finding, not driven: I did not create a failing write.
findings.impact: Same class as the P0 this round fixed: a per-document problem that stops the batch and leaves the documents behind it untouched. The record registers the missing-file case as F-B10R2-MISSINGFILE and explicitly says it is pre-existing; the artifact-write case is not mentioned anywhere.
findings.suggested_disposition: Fold (ii) into F-B10R2-MISSINGFILE's evaluation (already registered, and the record's description of it is correct apart from the line number), and add (i) as a second named item so the next pass evaluates the whole set rather than one instance.

adjudication_reason: All four findings I was asked to adjudicate as the round's core are really fixed, and I verified each one independently rather than by reading the author's evidence. P0 (B-VR-B10R2-01): the shared-column parse is now `metadata_state(document["metadata_json"])` at normalizer.py:1669, my own AST map finds no unguarded parse of that column left in normalize_catalog, and my own before/after driver shows the exact transition - `JSONDecodeError` from 1638 with nothing recorded on 5ec18a5, versus `escaped=false, completed=1` and an artifact carrying `metadata_unreadable` + `verdict: unverifiable` on f92fc71. I also re-applied the recorded M10 myself: the file still parses, the gate refuses it with a clean assertion, and the malformed-column abort really comes back on that mutated copy - a real kill of a real regression. P1-02: the false declaration is gone, the assertion that pinned it is gone (the only surviving string in tests/ is a HISTORY comment), and the registry counts (1 confirmed reader, 1 explicit non-chain reader, 12 scopes / 15 handoff sites) match a scanner I wrote myself to the digit. P1-03: across 8 unreadable values in both the dict and the real sqlite3.Row shape, HEAD adds the flag and downgrades the verdict where the pre-fix tree recorded a bare 'consistent'; empty and NULL stay unflagged, readable metadata still reaches the frontmatter, and ZR-502's 11 cases plus the three B10 files pass (35 passed), so the regression the author reported from his first attempt is genuinely gone. P3-06: the new hard rule really does refuse a direct reader placed in another product subpackage (RED with the file still parsing), and every GATE_BOUNDARIES number reproduces. The numbers are not inflated either: gate 15 cases, 10/10 killed by assertion, copy baseline 24 passed, 796 unit, and a contract collection of exactly the 1912 the CI log reports. I nevertheless return REJECT, on a live P2 that this round was specifically asked to hunt for and that the previous round's P0-fix narrative now obscures: `existing_metadata = json.loads(document["normalization_metadata_json"] or "{}")` at normalizer.py:1720 is the SAME defect shape on a sibling column - one document whose parse fails while its existing artifacts row carries malformed metadata raises JSONDecodeError out of `normalize_catalog`, and I measured that a HEALTHY document queued behind it is then never normalized at all (0 artifacts written). It is a one-line change to `metadata_state(...)`, in a module that already imports it for exactly this reason, and it is the difference between 'the P0 class is closed' and 'this instance of it is closed'. Alongside it, the CONFIRMED_DIRECT_READERS docstring still states the false reason that B-VR-B10R2-02 was raised about (that the parse sits in a failure path and produces a failure record - my probes show a malformed column produces a COMPLETED document), two comments and the record's §7quater still carry the now-wrong 13/16 handoff counts that this very commit invalidated, and the record's own disposition claims the file's numbers were updated to 15/10/1 while they appear nowhere in the body. None of that is fatal on its own; together with a live abort path that this round's own report does not mention, the honest verdict is that the fixes landed but the class is not closed. Step to reproduce the P2: build a throwaway catalog through CatalogStore with two documents and their `original_primary` locations, insert an `artifacts` row for the FIRST document with artifact_role='normalized', generator_name='source_catalog_normalizer', status='failed' and metadata_json='not json at all', make the first document's primary file absent from disk (so its parse fails), leave the second document healthy, then call normalize_catalog(config, store, force=True) - expect 'escaped: true, JSONDecodeError, normalizer.py:1720' and zero normalized.md on disk. My probe file is %TEMP%\b10vr4\v6_abort_hunt.py, scenarios S1/S4, with S3/S5 as controls. Before the round summary is finalized, two sentences in it need correcting as well: r4-final-status.md still carries 'COLUMN_VALUE_HANDOFFS 13 作用域 / 16 站点' (current: 12/15) and 'normalize_catalog 的解析不再能中止整轮' (not yet true for the sibling artifacts column), and the same 13/16 number and the retracted failure-path reason are still in read_chain.py's docstrings.
not_checked: The production catalog was never opened, so I cannot say how many real rows carry a malformed documents.metadata_json or artifacts.metadata_json. The blast radius of the fixed P0 and of my new P2 is demonstrated on synthetic catalogs, not measured against production data.
